mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to tightened financial conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the following 30 days
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the trigger period (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS rise is ≤0.25pp.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in PAYEMS (labor market employment) of at least 2% over the next month is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return, reflecting stronger consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥2% in the following 30 days
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat despite PAYEMS increase ≥2%, or the increase is <2%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both HOUST (industrial production) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 1% in the next 2 months predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return via improved business activity.
candidate_trigger: HOUST ↑1% and RSAFS ↑1% over next 60 days
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is negative despite both proxies rising by ≥1%, or the rise is not concurrent.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of 5% over the next quarter is associated with a negative S&P 20-day forward return due to supply-side weakness.
failure_condition: INDPRO declines <5% over the quarter or 20-day forward returns are positive during the decline.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4% for three consecutive months, the S&P 5-day forward return is expected to be positive as labor market tightness supports equity valuations.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive during the low-unemployment period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PAYEMS (job creation) of 10% in the next month combined with a rise in UNRATE (unemployment) above 5% predicts a negative S&P 60-day forward return due to recessionary labor market signals.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS ↓10% and UNRATE ↑ above 5% in the following 30 days
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative or the conditions do not co-occur as specified.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent CPIAUCSL (CPI) inflation above 3%, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to market anticipation of rate hikes.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or CPIAUCSL ≤3% during the period.

mechanism_narrative: When both GDPC1 (GDP) and INDPRO show consecutive monthly growth above 2% for two months, the S&P 60-day forward return is predicted to be positive due to robust economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 ↑2% and INDPRO ↑2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not positive or the growth conditions do not persist as required.
